parsedVerdict.reasoning:
PayrollService.ts only does work that belongs in the business (domain) layer. It enforces payroll rules: weekly hours must be 0–80, the employee must be active, and only approved timesheets go into a payslip. It coordinates domain objects (Timesheet.approve, Payslip.compute) and throws domain errors (PayrollRuleError, UnknownRecordError). It has no SQL, query building, connection or transaction handling, HTTP or request parsing, status codes, or framework logic.

It does use the concrete persistence repositories. That is an import and dependency-direction question, which is out of scope here. Turning repository records into domain objects (new Timesheet(r.id, ...), new Employee(...), e.contract as Contract) is light setup work that a domain service often does when it coordinates repositories. It is not storage logic.

RunContextDto has a 'Dto' suffix and an optional requestId, which hints at transport concerns. But it is only a passive type declaration. run() never reads it and no request-tracing or transport behaviour is carried out, so it is not a misplaced responsibility. No business rules leak out of their layer and no infrastructure or presentation logic leaks in. No ADR prose was given.
